Kessel-Niedrigwasser

A hazardous boiler condition where water level falls below the minimum safe mark, risking tube overheating, boiler damage, or explosion.

Questions and answers

Questions and answers

What is Kessel-Niedrigwasser?

In this glossary, Kessel-Niedrigwasser refers to: A hazardous boiler condition where water level falls below the minimum safe mark, risking tube overheating, boiler damage, or explosion.

How is Kessel-Niedrigwasser used in maritime?

In maritime communication, this term appears in contexts such as: "Chief Engineer, reagieren Sie auf den Niedrigwasser-Alarm des Kessels, indem Sie den Brenner sichern und den Wasserstand umgehend wiederherstellen."

Why does Kessel-Niedrigwasser matter in maritime?

Kessel-Niedrigwasser matters because it supports clear communication in Engineering contexts for Deck Officers, Engine Officers, and Masters. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as STCW, Marlins Test, ISF Watchkeeper, and GMDSS.

Who uses Kessel-Niedrigwasser?

Kessel-Niedrigwasser is mainly used by Deck Officers, Engine Officers, and Masters.

Definition

A hazardous boiler condition where water level falls below the minimum safe mark, risking tube overheating, boiler damage, or explosion.

Operational example

Chief engineer, respond to boiler low water alarm by securing burner and restoring water level without delay to prevent boiler damage.

Localized term

Kessel-Niedrigwasser

Localized example

Chief Engineer, reagieren Sie auf den Niedrigwasser-Alarm des Kessels, indem Sie den Brenner sichern und den Wasserstand umgehend wiederherstellen.
